column1: # Which released build a generation is swept with (#619, ADR 0073). One row per
# generation that runs a release rather than a build of the checkout; a
# generation with no row here builds the engine from HEAD the way g1 and g2 did.
# sha256 is the digest GitHub publishes for the asset, copied here before the
# sweep. This file is committed with the selection (the first of #619's three
# merges); the readers land with the defines (the second): sweep.sh will fetch
# the asset, refuse on a mismatch, unpack it in the zig-out layout under
# spike/unknown-rate/engine/<tag>/ (ignored by git) and mount that read-only at
# /work/zig-out, and apparatus.txt will then record the pin it checked against
# on a line of its own, beside the banner and the two digest lines the
# container computes from the mounted files; count.py check will refuse a
# complete generation that has a row here and no such line. Until that merge,
# nothing reads this file — it is the pin, written before the engine ran.
# The point of a release rather than a HEAD build: the selection is committed
# before any candidate runs, and main moves several times a day, so "the engine
# chosen before the sweep" has to be a thing that does not move with main.
